I always wanted to get into this when I was younger, but I never did. I figure I might as well start now. My question: How do I get started without spending a fortune? Are there 'beginner' rc aircraft I should be starting with? Are there any stores you recommend?

I got started by watching flitetest on youtube and buying the electronics through hobbyking.com.

It was very beneficial on two points -

  1. I understood how the plane was assembled and made - so when I crashed (You WILL crash!) I wasn't intimidated about repairing or rebuilding the whole thing. All together I think my first plane cost me $50 plus the transmitter.

  2. Since I wasn't intimidated about having to repair or remake - I flew more confidently and made faster growth of my skills that friends that started slightly before me. While they were too cautious to commit to a landing or takeoff with their new $300 plane, I was already in the air flying circles around them (Literally!)

For a first flitetest plane I would reccomend a FT Old Fogey or any other High wing Trainer plane.

my first advice is this - BE PREPARED TO CRASH. You will. Search on forums of flitetest.com or rcgroups.com and you can find people around you that will help you learn and get in the air safely.

If by some small world you are in the Reading, PA area let me know and I'll be happy to help you.
